hypothesis: A TeaCache threshold of 0.012 with a one-hit cap, selected before launch from round-3 signal distances, can reduce the aggressive 29-hit schedule to approximately nine hits and approach the conservative EasyCache round-2 time band while preserving the fixed-prompt visual trajectory.

build.tests: 9/9 CPU tests passed; py_compile, ledger validation, dry-run, git diff checks, lease UUID, GPU-idle, and shared-lock availability preflights passed. The optional DeepGEMM import warning remained the known benign environment condition.

run.signal_definition: relative mean-L1 change of token-subsampled first-block AdaLN-modulated hidden input, accumulated with identity rescaling
run.reuse_payload: separate conditional and unconditional full-block-stack residual histories

validity.visual_note: The first/middle/last frames remain very close to dense and EasyCache round 2: subject identity and anatomy, forest composition, and the increasing backlight trajectory are intact. Only slight pose, face, and background movement is visible, with no gross ghosting, duplication, deformation, or lighting break.

decision.reason: Retain as a valid conservative TeaCache calibration/frontier point: 10 genuine hits, 44.9 s total, and a passing lightweight visual screen. It is 2.81% faster than EasyCache round 2, so it is explicitly not the matched three-family comparison point.
